record.title: Cactus releases Needle 3, a laddered quantized model for offline tool use on small devices
record.summary: Cactus Compute released Needle 3 as a 2-bit, laddered model for local tool calling, structured extraction and text embeddings on devices ranging from phones to microcontrollers. The public model family spans 29–121 million parameters and 2–20 layer subnetworks, with the company describing 9–29 MB quantized variants and 8–29 MB package/model configurations. Cactus reports speed and benchmark advantages on mobile tool calling and structured extraction, but these comparisons come from its own tests and mix a CQ2 mobile binary, f16 baselines under vLLM and a hosted DeepSeek API. Independent matched accuracy, power, latency and real-use measurements remain open.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Cactus Compute publicly released a Needle 3 package, source repository and model/runtime materials for local tool calling and structured extraction; PyPI dates cactus-needle 3.0.0 to 2026-09-17.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Cactus describes Needle 3 as a 29–121M-parameter laddered model with deployable 2–20-layer subnetworks, CQ2 quantization and 9–29 MB model variants; its page also reports Raspberry Pi 5 speed ranges.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Cactus reports that Needle 3 beats models ten times its size on mobile tool calls and matches models two to three times its size on extraction across vendor-selected evaluation suites. The comparison does not use a uniform hardware, precision or hosted-versus-local regime.

evidence_gaps.description: The public comparison is vendor-run and uses mixed precision and serving regimes; independent matched accuracy and latency are unknown.
No independent power, thermal, memory or sustained-throughput measurements on the intended phone, wearable, robot or microcontroller deployment classes were checked.
The provenance and domain coverage of Cactus’s proprietary structured training set are not public in the release materials reviewed.

brief.importance_rationale: If local schema-constrained tool use can approach substantially larger systems at single-digit to tens-of-megabytes model sizes, it matters for offline products, device privacy and inference cost across large installed bases. The score is notable because the claimed task performance is narrow and vendor-evaluated; no independent deployment benefit has yet been established.
limitations: All Needle 3 benchmark and speed figures inspected here are reported by Cactus Compute; no independent reproduction or matched test was performed.
The tool-calling and extraction suites are narrow. Performance does not establish general reasoning, reliable autonomous action or broad assistant capability.
The comparisons mix a 2-bit CQ2 Needle binary, f16 baselines under vLLM and a hosted DeepSeek V4 Flash API, so size/accuracy claims do not isolate parameter count or hardware efficiency.
Fine-tuning gains are vendor-reported using proprietary data and small downstream test sets; no independent held-out or cross-product evaluation was inspected.
Power draw, thermal behavior, sustained throughput, peak memory on named low-end devices and end-to-end application failure rates remain unmeasured independently.
Cactus states that the 360B-token structured training set is proprietary; data composition and training ablations are not available for review.
brief.summary: Cactus Compute released Needle 3 as a 2-bit, laddered model for local tool calling, structured extraction and text embeddings on devices ranging from phones to microcontrollers. The public model family spans 29–121 million parameters and 2–20 layer subnetworks, with the company describing 9–29 MB quantized variants and 8–29 MB package/model configurations. Cactus reports speed and benchmark advantages on mobile tool calling and structured extraction, but these comparisons come from its own tests and mix a CQ2 mobile binary, f16 baselines under vLLM and a hosted DeepSeek API. Independent matched accuracy, power, latency and real-use measurements remain open.

technical.claimed_result: Cactus reports mobile tool-call performance above models ten times larger and extraction performance comparable to models two to three times larger. It reports 400–4,000 decode tokens/s and 1,000–10,000 prefill tokens/s on Raspberry Pi 5. Its public page says CQ2 Needle variants are compared with f16 baselines running through vLLM and hosted DeepSeek V4 Flash, and reports additional fine-tuned gains on 200 DroidCall examples and a 961-row Mobile Actions set.
technical.compute_or_cost: Cactus reports 9–29 MB CQ2 model binaries (and describes 8–29 MB configurations), with deployment engines under 1 MB. The company states 360 billion tokens of proprietary structured training data. No independent energy, peak-memory, unit-cost or cloud-versus-local total-cost comparison was conducted.
technical.demonstrated_result: A public implementation, PyPI package and model/runtime artifacts are available. PyPI records the first 3.0.0 package release on 2026-09-17; the current product page and repository document model architecture, deployment package, and evaluation setup. the research desk did not independently execute the model or reproduce its results.
technical.implementation_status: Public package, Apache-2.0 repository, quantized weights and prebuilt engines are offered for multiple platforms. A public package release is verified; target-device execution and third-party product adoption were not independently tested.
technical.mechanism: A Laddered Simple Attention Network with Monarch Hadamard MLP blocks, grouped-query attention with causal convolution taps, n-gram engram memory and multi-lane hyper-connections. Every depth from 2 to 20 layers is exported as its own subnetwork; constrained decoding compiles supplied tool or extraction schemas into a byte-level grammar.
technical.novelty: The model is explicitly trained and exported as a capacity ladder: multiple deployable subnetworks share an architecture and runtime, targeting constrained local tool selection and schema-constrained structured outputs rather than general chat.
technical.regime: Vendor-selected tool-calling and extraction suites, including exact-call/exact-order and field-level F1 metrics. Fine-tuning results use the vendor’s platform, proprietary data and small downstream test sets. Raspberry Pi 5 speed figures are vendor-reported.
technical.reproducibility: Source code and deployment artifacts are public, but the training corpus is proprietary and the published benchmark values are vendor-authored. Independent reruns under matched tasks, hardware, quantization and inference budgets remain open.
technical.strongest_baseline: For base-model evaluation, the vendor compares against larger models on Mobile Actions (961 rows), DroidCall (200 rows), BFCL v4 (3,641 rows), DSTC8 extraction (1,813 turns) and SNIPS extraction (700 rows per setting). This is not a fully matched hardware/precision regime: Needle uses its shipped CQ2 binary, comparison baselines use f16 under vLLM, and DeepSeek V4 Flash is called through a cloud API.

brief.title: Cactus releases Needle 3, a laddered quantized model for offline tool use on small devices
brief.why_it_matters: A small, deployable model that returns schema-constrained actions could move some tool use from cloud calls onto devices with tight memory or intermittent connectivity. If the reported size and task performance hold on target hardware, this changes the local inference design space; current evidence establishes a released implementation and vendor-run results, not independent device utility or broad capability.
